1.title: Claude Features: Chat, Search, Thinking, Research, Files and Artifacts
1.text: Welcome to Module six: Claude Features: Chat, Search, Thinking, Research, Files and Artifacts. This module covers claude features: chat, search, thinking, research, files and artifacts. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. The main features of Claude and what each is for. How to choose the lightest feature that fits the task. The difference between web search, extended thinking and Research. What you can do with files, Projects, Artifacts, Skills and connectors.

1.title: Case Check-In: Cedarbrook's Monday Requests
1.text: Our running case is Cedarbrook Outfitters. Cedarbrook's Monday Requests. Customer care wants a quick reply draft. Finance wants a board-ready analysis of regional returns from a spreadsheet. Marketing wants a competitor price scan with sources. Operations wants a standing assistant that knows the packing procedures. Each request needs a different feature.

1.title: The Feature Map
1.text: The Feature Map. The figure shows this: Claude features grouped by purpose: one-off help in chat, grounded help with search, Research and files, and standing setup with Projects, Skills and connectors.

1.title: The Feature Map, continued
1.text: The Feature Map, continued. Chat. What it does: Conversation with Claude. Use it for: Drafting, explaining, brainstorming, quick edits. Web search. What it does: Looks up live web content; gives citations. Use it for: Simple, current facts needing one or two lookups. Extended thinking. What it does: Claude reasons through the problem before answering. Use it for: Hard reasoning with no need for recent web data: math, logic, debugging, multi-angle analysis. Research. What it does: Multi-step investigation across the web and your connected tools; produces a cited report. Use it for: Comprehensive gathering (about five or more lookups, a few minutes). File upload. What it does: Reads P D F, D O C X, C S V, T X T, X L S X and more, plus images. Use it for: Summaries, analysis and Q and A on your documents.

1.title: The Feature Map, continued
1.text: The Feature Map, continued. Create and edit files. What it does: Builds Excel, Word, Power Point and P D F files in a sandbox. Use it for: Reports, slide decks, spreadsheets, charts. Artifacts. What it does: Side-panel content you can edit, reuse and share. Use it for: Documents, slides, dashboards, small tools. Projects. What it does: A workspace with instructions and knowledge for many chats. Use it for: Recurring work needing the same background (Module eleven). Memory and chat search. What it does: Remembers context across chats; finds past chats. Use it for: Continuity (Module eight). Skills. What it does: Reusable procedures Claude loads when relevant. Use it for: Repeatable tasks with a set method (Module twelve).

1.title: The Feature Map, continued
1.text: The Feature Map, continued. Connectors. What it does: Link Claude to apps such as Google Drive, Gmail, Slack. Use it for: Working with your own data and tools (Module twelve). Exam tip: Choose the lightest feature that fits the task. Research for a one-line fact, or plain chat for a competitor report, are both mismatches.

1.title: Search, Thinking and Research
1.text: Search, Thinking and Research. The figure shows this: Web search for quick current facts, extended thinking for hard reasoning, Research for comprehensive cited reports.

1.title: Search, Thinking and Research, continued
1.text: Search, Thinking and Research, continued. Best for. Web search: A current fact: news, a price, company info. Extended thinking: Complex reasoning without needing the web. Research: Deep, multi-source investigation. Typical effort. Web search: One or two tool calls. Extended thinking: Claude thinks longer before answering. Research: Five or more lookups, about one to three minutes. Output. Web search: Short answer with citations. Extended thinking: A reasoned answer. Research: A longer report with citations. Sources. Web search: Web. Extended thinking: Your prompt and what Claude knows. Research: Web plus your connected tools (for example Google Workspace).

1.title: Search, Thinking and Research, continued
1.text: Search, Thinking and Research, continued. Examples. Web search: "What is the current return window at a rival?". Extended thinking: "Optimize this packing schedule", "find the logic error in this formula". Research: "Compare five rivals' pricing and warranty terms and recommend a position". Web search must be available to Claude; on Team and Enterprise plans an owner enables it for the workspace first. On some versions Claude decides when to search; you can always say "search the web" or "do not search".

1.title: Search, Thinking and Research, continued
1.text: Search, Thinking and Research, continued. Research is a paid-plan feature; it uses more of your usage limit because it retrieves many sources. On mobile it may search only the web and skip connectors. Research plus thinking: thinking plans the approach and Research carries out the gathering. For all three, verify what you will rely on (Module four). Exam tip: Key words: "current fact" points to web search; "reason through" or "complex logic" points to extended thinking; "comprehensive report with sources" points to Research.

1.title: Files, Projects, Artifacts and More
1.text: Files, Projects, Artifacts and More. File upload. Supported documents include P D F, D O C X, C S V, T X T, H T M L, O D T, R T F, E P U B, Jason (Java Script Object Notation) and X L S X; images include J P E G, P N G, G I F and Web P. In a chat: up to twenty files, five hundred megabytes each; P D F s up to one thousand pages (one hundred pages or fewer: text and visuals are analyzed; one hundred one to one thousand: text only). Split very large documents. Non-P D F documents yield text only, so embedded images are not read.

1.title: Files, Projects, Artifacts and More, continued
1.text: Files, Projects, Artifacts and More, continued. Create and edit files. With Create and edit files (code execution) on, Claude builds Excel, Word, Power Point and P D F files, writes scripts and makes charts in a private sandbox. Files can be downloaded or saved to Google Drive (about thirty megabytes). File creation uses more of your usage limit. Artifacts. For substantial, reusable content such as documents, slides, designs and small tools (Module five). Projects. Standing instructions plus a knowledge base for related chats. Prefer a Project over re-pasting the same background (Module eleven).

2.title: Files, Projects, Artifacts and More, continued
2.text: Files, Projects, Artifacts and More, continued. Skills. Folders of instructions loaded only when relevant; ideal for a repeatable method such as "our report format" (Module twelve). Connectors. Give Claude access to Google Drive, Gmail, Calendar and other services within your permissions (Module twelve). Images. Claude can read images, charts and screenshots. It does not create photos or illustrations like an image generator; it can build diagrams and charts. Names, plan availability and limits move quickly. The principle holds: match the feature to the need.

2.title: A Feature Chooser
2.text: A Feature Chooser. The figure shows this: A feature chooser: current facts to web search, hard reasoning to extended thinking, comprehensive report to Research, your files to upload, repeated context to a Project, reusable output to an artifact, repeatable method to a Skill.

2.title: A Feature Chooser, continued
2.text: A Feature Chooser, continued. A quick draft or explanation. Chat. A single current fact. Web search. A hard logic or math problem. Extended thinking (and verify). A cited, multi-source report. Research. Questions about your documents. File upload (or a Project). The same background every week. Project. A deliverable people will edit or share. Artifact or file. The same method every time. Skill. Data in Drive or Gmail. Connector. Exam tip: Connectors, web search and Research widen what Claude can see and use more of your limit, so turn on only what the task needs.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Principle: Lightest feature that fits. Web search: Current facts; one or two lookups; citations. Extended thinking: Hard reasoning; no web needed. Research: Five or more lookups, about one to three minutes; cited report; web plus connectors; paid plans. Files: Up to twenty per chat, five hundred megabytes each. Create files: Excel, Word, Power Point, P D F; Create and edit files must be on. Artifacts: Reusable, editable, shareable content. Projects: Standing instructions and knowledge. Skills: Repeatable procedures loaded when relevant. Images: Reads images; does not generate photos.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A marketer needs the current published price of one competitor product. Which feature fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. A simple current fact needs one or two lookups.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. A strategist wants a comprehensive, cited comparison of five rivals' pricing, warranty and shipping terms. Which feature fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Research handles multi-step, multi-source investigation with a cited report.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. An analyst must find the logic error in a complicated discount rule that needs no outside data. Which feature helps most? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Hard reasoning with no need for current web facts is the use case for extended thinking.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A team lead pastes the same eight hundred-word brand-voice guide at the start of every chat. What is the better setup? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Standing context that is needed again and again belongs in a Project, so every chat starts with the same background without pasting.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A user uploads a one thousand five hundred-page P D F and sees a "file too large" error. What should they do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. P D F s over one thousand pages cannot be uploaded; split large documents.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Select two. Which two tasks are best done with Create and edit files? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and B. File creation builds Office and P D F files from your material.

2.title: Practice Question 7
2.text: Question seven. A manager asks Claude to paint a realistic photo of a tent in the mountains. What is true? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Image generation is not a Claude capability; reading images and building diagrams is.

2.title: Practice Question 8
2.text: Question eight. Which request is the poorest match to Research? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. A quick lookup does not need a multi-minute investigation.

2.title: Practice Question 9
2.text: Question nine. Why might a team limit the use of Research and file creation on busy days? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Multi-step tools and file creation use more of your allowance.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all nine answers. Question one: A. Question two: C. Question three: A. Question four: C. Question five: A. Question six: A and B. Question seven: C. Question eight: D. Question nine: B. In the next module, we continue the course.
